label: certificate rotation
type: replacing a cluster's certificates without downtime - node certificates one at a time under a newly uploaded CA, with the old CA removed last. Requires no restart of the cluster or of any node since 7.1.
evidence: This may be used during CA certificate rotation: a new CA is uploaded, node certificates are changed one by one, and finally, the old CA is removed.
Certificate-rotation on the server-side does not require that either the cluster or any of its nodes be restarted.
No root or intermediate certificate should ever be used to issue certificates with an expiration date later than that of the issuer itself.
note: The multiple-CA capability added in 7.1 exists in order to make this procedure possible - the reference page (using-multiple-cas.md) states the capability, the procedure states the ordering that uses it, and neither alone tells an administrator how to rotate a CA safely. Round 26 also recorded what all three certificate pages omit: no revocation mechanism (CRL or OCSP) is documented anywhere in the scope, which is filed as a docs-issue.
